related_questions.question: What is the difference between final action dates and dates for filing?

text_blocks.snippet: The Visa Bulletin uses two key dates to manage the availability of immigrant visas: Final Action Dates and Dates for Filing. Final Action Dates determine when a visa number is available for issuance, meaning when a green card can actually be approved. Dates for Filing, on the other hand, indicate the earliest point when applicants can submit their adjustment of status applications, even if a visa number isn't immediately available. In essence, Final Action Dates dictate when the green card is issued, while Dates for Filing determine when you can file your application for the green card process.
snippet_highlighted_words: Final Action Dates dictate when the green card is issued, while Dates for Filing determine when you can file your application for the green card process

list.title: Final Action Dates:
list.snippet: This chart shows the dates when immigrant visas are available for issuance. If your priority date (your place in the visa queue) is earlier than the date listed for your category, you are eligible to receive a green card.

list.title: Dates for Filing:
list.snippet: This chart indicates the earliest date when applicants can submit their Form I-485 (Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status). This allows applicants to file earlier, potentially gaining benefits like work permits (EAD) and travel authorization (AP) while waiting for their final green card approval.
Final Action Dates are when the final decision on your green card application is made, and you receive your green card.
Dates for Filing are when you can start the process of applying for a green card, even if the final approval will take longer.

USCIS (United States Citizenship and Immigration Services) will announce each month which chart (Dates for Filing or Final Action Dates) they will use for processing adjustment of status applications.

It's common for the Dates for Filing to be earlier than the Final Action Dates, allowing applicants to file their applications sooner and potentially receive benefits like work permits while waiting for their visa number to become available.
The Visa Bulletin is updated monthly by the Department of State (DOS).
You can find the most current Visa Bulletin on the DOS website.

related_questions.question: What is the processing time for EB-1?

text_blocks.snippet: EB-1 visa processing times vary, but generally include an initial I-140 petition (average 7.7 months) and then an I-485 application for adjustment of status (average 6.9 months if already in the US). Premium processing can expedite the I-140 to 15 days. However, the overall green card process can take 1.5 to 2 years, or longer for some countries.
snippet_highlighted_words: 1.5 to 2 years, or longer for some countries

list.title: Standard Processing:
list.snippet: The I-140 (Immigrant Petition for Alien Worker) typically takes around 7.7 months to be processed.

list.title: Premium Processing:
list.snippet: If you opt for premium processing, you can get a decision on the I-140 within 15 business days.

list.title: If already in the US:
list.snippet: The I-485 application for adjustment of status (to become a permanent resident) is the next step after the I-140 is approved, and it generally takes about 6.9 months according to Boundless Immigration.

list.title: If outside the US:
list.snippet: You would apply for an immigrant visa through consular processing, and the timeline will depend on visa availability and the processing times of the National Visa Center and the specific embassy or consulate.

list.title: USCIS Workload:
list.snippet: The overall volume of applications at USCIS can impact processing times.

list.title: EB-1 Category:
list.snippet: Different EB-1 subcategories (Extraordinary Ability, Outstanding Professor/Researcher, Multinational Manager) may have varying processing times.

list.title: Service Center:
list.snippet: The USCIS service center handling your case can also influence processing times.

list.title: Completeness of Application:
list.snippet: A well-prepared application with all necessary documentation will expedite the process.

list.title: Priority Dates:
list.snippet: For some countries, visa availability (priority dates) may cause delays in the final green card issuance.
Premium processing for the I-140 is available for an additional fee and can significantly reduce the processing time.
It is particularly useful for EB-1 applicants in managerial or executive capacities, as it expedites the path to permanent residency according to the Immigration Law Group.

text_blocks.snippet: In Summary: While EB-1 processing can be faster than other employment-based green card categories, it still involves multiple steps and various factors can affect the overall timeline. Premium processing can help expedite the initial I-140 petition, but the overall process can still take several months to over a year.
